title: Tenant Onboarding: VPC ↔ Air‑Gapped Packaging & Day‑2 Orchestration Playbook
author: Anya Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents a repeatable, customer-facing operational procedure for onboarding tenants that require mixed connectivity: a VPC-hosted control plane with tenant inference workers behind an air‑gapped perimeter (air‑gapped or strict egress VPC). It covers packaging and signing artifacts, the bridge/orchestrator pattern (edge‑bridge), network preflight, canary upgrade choreography, rollback criteria, and Day‑2 operational checks. The intent is to standardize operator actions, reduce risk during upgrades and handoffs, and capture customer requirements for compliance evidence.

Use cases this covers:
- Customers who want Redwood control plane in our VPC but model runners on customer network (air‑gapped).
- Branch office or on‑prem tenants that receive periodic signed bundles and a thin bridge for telemetry/metric aggregation.
- Regulated customers requiring locally‑executed inference with external routing fallback disabled.

Key goals and SLOs:
- Onboarding success: complete deployment, smoke tests green, and evidence artifacts provided within 5 business days (timebox configurable per contract).
- Runtime availability: tenant control-plane reachability 99.9% (per SLA) and local inference node 99.95% in-region (customer dependent).
- Latency budget (internal target): 95th percentile tail < 250ms for control-plane RPCs when on the same region/private network.

Owners and roles:
- Owner (Redwood): Deployment Engineering (eng-private-deployments); primary contact: Anya Patel.
content_2:
High level architecture summary:

- redwood-control-plane (hosted, VPC) — control plane and orchestration APIs.
- edge-bridge (customer‑deployed lightweight service) — TLS‑mutual bridge allowing metric/health check collection and secure bundle exchange.
- private-agent (customer side) — runtime agent that unpacks signed bundles, configures local runtime and model artifacts, and participates in canary/rollout handshakes.
- rpm-packager / docker-bundle-signer — Redwood internal packaging pipeline that produces signed, reproducible release bundles for air‑gapped installs.

Network model (patterns):
1) Pull mode (preferred for occasional reconnects): edge-bridge initiates TLS mTLS to control plane only to fetch new signed bundles; outbound required but limited to specific FQDNs and ports.
2) Push mode (for strictly egress‑blocked sites): Operator ships physical media or S3 transfer via customer‑approved staging, then private-agent validates signatures and installs locally.

Preflight checklist (operator):
1) Validate customer environment meets minimum HW: 8×A100/40GB or equivalent for production tenant, or N vCPU with quantized runtime for smaller tenants. (See Hardware matrix table.)
2) Confirm network ACLs/NGFW rules allow bridge egress to: control.redwood-inference.net:443 and s3.redwood-inference.net:443 (or provide alternate mirror endpoints).
3) KMS/HSM: confirm customer KMS integration option and key IDs for envelope encryption.
4) Time sync: ensure NTP configured and drift < 2s.
5) ID and rotate maintenance window with customer.

Hardware matrix (operator quick table):
| Tier | GPUs | Min RAM | Disk | Use case |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| small | 1×A10 or 4×T4 | 64GB | 1TB NVMe | dev/proof-of-concept |
| medium | 4×A100‑40GB | 256GB | 4TB NVMe | production small tenants |
| large | 8×A100‑80GB | 512GB | 8TB NVMe + shared storage | high throughput, multi-tenant |

Artifact packaging and signing:
- We produce two artifact types: OCI image bundles (for containerized private-agent + runtime) and .tar.gz signed model bundles (weights + config + quantization metadata).
- Packaging steps (CI pipeline):
  1. Build base images with immutable tags: e.g., registry.redwood-inference.net/private-agent:v2026-01-10
  2. Run image scanners and SBOM generation.
  3. Create signed model bundle: sha256sum model.tar.gz -> sign with internal release key; create accompanying signed manifest.json (manifest fields: model_name, revision, sha256, q8_profile).
  4. Publish to secure artifact repo and mirror for airgap.

Signing checklist (operator & security):
- Ensure RPM/DEB and OCI signatures verified using release public key (GPG and cosign).
- Manifest.json example (signed):
{
  "model_name": "redwood-vari-bf16",
  "revision": "2026-01-02",
  "sha256": "...",
  "q_profile": "int8-s2",
  "signed_by": "release-team@redwood.com"
}

Installation modes (operator flows):
1) Automated edge-bridge install (recommended):
  - Operator provides one-time bootstrap token created in control-plane UI.
  - On customer host: curl -fsSL https://packages.redwood-inference.net/bootstrap.sh | sudo BRIDGE_TOKEN=XXX bash
  - The bootstrap script installs private-agent, creates systemd service, and performs initial health checks.
  - Sample systemd unit snippet:
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Private Agent
After=network.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/private-agent --config /etc/redwood/agent.yaml
Restart=on-failure
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

2) Manual airgap install (no egress):
  - Operator prepares signed bundles and image tarballs.
  - On site: load images (docker load --input private-agent.tar.gz), verify cosign signature, and run private-agent with --airgap flag.

Canary upgrade choreography (step by step):
1) Create a canary tenant slice (1–5% of traffic) in the control plane for the new bundle.
2) Publish signed bundle and stage to mirror/edge-bridge.
3) Schedule a maintenance window (if required).
4) Promote canary: instruct selected private-agent instances to fetch bundle with control-plane API: POST /v1/agent/commands {"action": "apply_bundle", "bundle_id": "b-2026-02-01" }
5) Monitor:
   - Health: agent heartbeat every 30s, new bundle activation logs streamed to control plane.
   - Metrics: model_latency_p50/p95, model_mem_pressure, kv_cache_hit_rate.
   - Telemetry SLO: bundle activation must complete within 10 minutes on canary agents or the canary is aborted.
6) Wait for metric stabilization window (default 60 minutes).
7) Roll forward or rollback: see rollback criteria below.

Rollback criteria (automated and manual):
- Automated rollback triggers when any of the following happen on more than 20% of canary hosts within the stabilization window:
  - model_latency_p95 increases by > 35% and absolute increase > 150ms
  - model_error_rate (runtime exceptions or invalid outputs) > 0.5%
  - memory OOMs or repeated restarts > 3 in 30 minutes
- Manual rollback: operator can trigger POST /v1/agent/commands {"action": "rollback", "target_bundle": "previous" }

Post‑upgrade validation checklist (Day‑2):
- Confirm agent version and bundle revision via control-plane UI or API.
- Run smoke prompt set (internal test prompts and customer-provided golden prompts). Capture outputs and diff against baseline with allowable fuzz thresholds (documented per-customer).
- Check KV cache hit rate and prefix reuse metrics > configured baseline.
- Verify auditable logs exist for bundle signatures and time of install (for compliance).

Observability and alerts (suggested):
- Alerts to create (example):
  - agent.offline for > 5m (severity: P2)
  - bundle.apply.failure.rate > 1% across tenant hosts in 30m (severity: P1)
  - model.latency.p95 > 350ms for 10m (severity: P1)
  - disk.space.available < 10% on primary NVMe (severity: P2)

Evidence and compliance artifacts to deliver to customer:
- Signed manifest.json and release public key fingerprint.
- SBOM and vulnerability scan report for the private-agent image.
- Installation logs and systemd journal export during bundle application.
- Acceptance test report (smoke prompts + diff).

Common troubleshooting recipes (quick examples):
1) Private agent fails to fetch bundle over bridge:
   - Check edge-bridge certificate chain and mTLS trust store. Command: openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-inference.net:443 -showcerts
   - Verify bootstrap token is valid and not revoked in control-plane.
2) Model memory OOM after upgrade:
   - Revert to previous bundle if immediate fix needed.
   - Inspect model manifest for quantization profile mismatch (q_profile).
   - If repeated, open "runtime-kernel" incident with eng-serving-runtime and attach heap profile.

Customer requirements matrix (what to collect during sales->onboarding):
- Networking: outbound allowlist endpoints, IP ranges, required ports.
- Security: KMS/HSM choice, customer responsible key IDs, and audit retention window.
- Hardware: GPU list, NVMe size, networking bandwidth.
- Compliance: any data egress restrictions, required evidence types, breach notification SLA.
- Maintenance window: preferred windows and blackout periods.
- Acceptance test set: golden prompts and success thresholds.

Sample commands and snippets:
- Create one-time bootstrap token (control-plane CLI):
  redwoodctl tokens create --purpose bootstrap --expires 72h --tenant-id t-12345

- Agent API check (curl):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_TOKEN" https://localhost:8081/v1/agent/status | jq

- Example minimal agent.yaml:
  server_url: https://control.redwood-inference.net
  tls: { ca_file: /etc/redwood/ca.pem, cert_file: /etc/redwood/cert.pem, key_file: /etc/redwood/key.pem }
  bundle_dir: /var/lib/redwood/bundles
  mode: airgap # pull | push | airgap

Operational handoff checklist (before closure):
1) Confirm customer acceptance tests passed and documented.
2) Deliver compliance evidence bundle and SBOM.
3) Create maintenance playbook for customer (contact points, escalation).
4) Schedule QBR and hand over to Customer Success; assign a monthly health check cadence.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Release signing guide: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/container-image-signing-and-verification-playbook-2026.json
- Acceptance test templates: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-acceptance-and-smoke-validation-2026.json
- Runtime incident playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-oom-and-crashplaybook-2025.json

If you are executing this playbook for a new customer, follow the Preflight checklist, create a dedicated runbook in the customer folder (link it from related_pages), and add the customer-specific acceptance thresholds to the canary configuration before the first bundle rollout.
